correctness.rationale: The q_i edges are pairwise disjoint so Q={q_1,...,q_n} is a simplex of the matching complex, which is flag. The standard star-cluster lemma (Donovan--Scoville Proposition 2.5) says the union C of closed stars of vertices of any simplex in a flag complex is simplicially collapsible. For any matching, if common c is present all q_i are compatible. Otherwise at most one page p_i meets u and at most one r_j meets v, and q_k conflicts exactly with p_k or r_k; at most two indices are blocked. Thus n≥3 entails every matching face belongs to C, proving actual simplicial collapsibility. At n=2 the two edges {p_1,r_2} and {p_2,r_1} are precisely the missing cells, attached by their endpoints to collapsible C; collapsing C gives two independent loops, hence S¹∨S¹. At n=1 the matching complex is the disjoint pair of edges {c,q_1} and {p_1,r_1}, hence S⁰. Independent direct all-matching enumeration n=1..5 matches face vectors and star-cluster outside faces, while the uniform blocked-index proof supplies arbitrary n.

originality.rationale: Donovan--Scoville develop the star-cluster tool and compute Dutch windmills sharing a vertex, not edge-sharing C4 books. Bayer--Jelić Milutinović--Vega polygonal line tilings allow successive shared edges but forbid three polygons meeting; the entire n≥3 book violates that condition. Their outerplanar framework likewise does not cover n≥3 because the book contains a subdivided K_(2,3). The sharp transition at three pages and explicit homotopy types are not statements of those inspected theorems. The finite n=1,2 boundary is still accounted for, and novelty is best knowledge with the Resultary outage and terminology risks.
